title: Single-Point Scanner
one_liner: List your critical deals, systems and decisions, and see which ones depend on one person with nothing written down.
speaker: Salim
context: Salim guessed that the board pushed Jensen out partly over nepotism, no signed contracts with major partners, everything centred on one person and no succession plan. In his telling, the board wanted things written down and signed.
demo: The owner fills in a table of rows: deal, system or decision; who holds it; whether it's signed or documented; whether there's a backup person; and how much revenue depends on it. The tool scores each row, ranks the single points of failure, gives a 'one person out for two weeks' exposure total, and produces a printable action list. An example company is preloaded.
data_plan: Entirely the customer's own input, stored in the browser's local storage. Scoring rules are bundled and shown on the page.
risks: Founders may not want to spend time on it until a crisis hits. Writing deals down can surface disputes. Must not drift into legal contract drafting; hand that off to the client's lawyer.

figures.meaning: how long Jensen was out as NVIDIA CEO
figures.said: Jensen was out for 11 days, 264 hours

acceptance: Adding a row with 'no backup person' and 'not documented' moves it to the top of the ranked list with a red flag
The exposure total updates live as revenue-at-risk values are edited
The 'Load example' button fills in a sample company and labels it as an example
Clicking Print or Export shows a clean one-page action list
On a 375px-wide screen the table becomes stacked cards with no sideways scrolling

opportunity.title: Head-Only Inventory
opportunity.one_liner: A fixed-fee sprint that finds every deal, password and decision living only in a founder's head, then writes it down.
opportunity.customer: Founder-led US companies with 10–150 staff, especially ones preparing for a fundraise, sale or bank loan, where the owner holds key partner relationships personally
opportunity.problem: Key customer and supplier deals rest on handshakes. Critical knowledge and logins sit with one person, and nobody has a plan for when that person is out. Investors, buyers and lenders mark the company down for it, and an emergency absence can stall the business.
opportunity.revenue_model: Fixed-fee sprint at about $3,500–$7,500 per company, plus an optional $300 a month to keep the register up to date (estimate)
opportunity.why_now: The episode describes the world's most valuable company thrown into chaos over unsigned deals and no succession plan. That makes key-person risk an easy story to sell, and AI interview and transcription tools now let one consultant turn a founder's knowledge into documents quickly.
